title: The Pager

lines.text: A man left his pager at home.
In the evening he comes back and reads his messages.
The first one:
Sweetie, darling, my love, please call me.
Kisses, always yours, Marina.
The second one:
I already called, you don't have to worry.
Your wife.

notes: Both messages kept in full with 'die erste / die zweite'. The pager stays as a retro detail in the narration, the phone prop plays it. The mistress is shown in the bottom half of a split screen while she sends her message; the wife waits on the sofa and voices her own message.
title: Der Pager

lines.text: Ein Mann hat seinen Pager zu Hause vergessen.
Am Abend kommt er zurück und liest die Nachrichten.
Die erste:
Schatz, Liebster, mein Geliebter, ruf mich bitte an.
Küsschen, für immer deine Marina.
Die zweite:
Ich habe schon angerufen, du musst dir keine Sorgen machen.
Deine Frau.

notes: Whole story kept: the wife's order turned into her own line, the walk into the forest, the days of waiting, the cat coming home first and the man right behind. Three scenes: home, forest, home again. 'На хрен' softened to 'на фиг'.
title: Кот в лесу

lines.text: У одного мужика был кот.
И то ли старый котяра уже стал, то ли сметану спёр, но жена мужика приказала:
Отнеси его далеко в лес и оставь там на произвол судьбы!
Делать нечего — понёс мужик кота в лес.
И сам пропал.
День его нет, два нет,
на третий день появляется дома кот,
и тут же мужик следом — грязный, злой и голодный.
Ну ты чего, урод, отнёс кота в лес?
Ага, отнёс, блин!
И если бы за ним следом не пошёл, заблудился бы на фиг...
lines.uncensored: И если бы за ним следом не пошёл, заблудился бы на хрен...

notes: Whole story kept: the wife's order turned into her own line, the walk into the forest, the days of waiting, the cat coming home first and the man right behind. Three scenes: home, forest, home again. 'На хрен' rendered as 'lost as hell', softened to 'heck'.
title: The Cat in the Forest

lines.text: A man had a cat.
And whether the old tomcat had just got too old, or he had swiped the sour cream, the man's wife ordered:
Take him far into the forest and leave him there to his fate!
Nothing to be done — the man carried the cat into the forest.
And went missing himself.
One day he's gone, two days he's gone,
on the third day the cat shows up at home,
and right behind him the man — dirty, angry and hungry.
Well, you freak, did you take the cat to the forest?
Yeah, I took him, dang it!
And if I hadn't followed him back, I'd have got lost as heck...
lines.uncensored: And if I hadn't followed him back, I'd have got lost as hell...

notes: Whole story kept: the wife's order turned into her own line, the walk into the forest, the days of waiting, the cat coming home first and the man right behind. Three scenes: home, forest, home again. 'Verdammt noch mal' carries 'на хрен' and needs no softening.
title: Der Kater im Wald

lines.text: Ein Mann hatte einen Kater.
Und ob der alte Kater nun einfach zu alt geworden war oder die saure Sahne geklaut hatte, jedenfalls befahl die Frau des Mannes:
Bring ihn weit in den Wald und überlass ihn dort seinem Schicksal!
Da war nichts zu machen — der Mann trug den Kater in den Wald.
Und verschwand selbst.
Einen Tag ist er weg, zwei Tage ist er weg,
am dritten Tag taucht zu Hause der Kater auf,
und gleich hinter ihm der Mann — dreckig, wütend und hungrig.
Na, du Blödmann, hast du den Kater in den Wald gebracht?
Ja, hab ich, Mensch!
Und wenn ich ihm nicht hinterhergelaufen wäre, hätte ich mich verdammt noch mal verlaufen...

notes: All narration and lines kept, the friend's plea split into two lines. The call is a split screen: the hungover man in bed on top, the friend at the police station below. After he hangs up, a cut to the bedroom alone; both men wear red noses and stubble so the wife's look at his face pays off.
title: Выручай, друг

lines.text: Мужик утром просыпается с глубочайшего похмелья от телефонного звонка.
Звонит друг, которого он давно не видел.
Ты откуда?
Выручай, друг, из вытрезвителя звоню, недалеко от твоего дома.
Денег нет, надо сто пятьдесят шесть рублей, чтобы отпустили.
Мужик обещает, кладёт трубку и, собрав остаток сил, поднимается и начинает медленно одеваться, стараясь не упасть.
Куда?!
Тот честно объясняет ситуацию.
Жена пристально смотрит на его опухшую физиономию и говорит:
Триста двенадцать рублей возьми!

notes: Sobering-up station is the drunk tank; 156 and 312 roubles became 56 and 112 dollars to keep the doubling. All narration and lines kept. Split-screen call, then a cut to the bedroom; both men wear red noses and stubble so the wife's look at his face pays off.
title: Bail Money

lines.text: One morning a man wakes up with the deepest hangover of his life to the phone ringing.
It's a friend he hasn't seen for ages.
Where are you calling from?
Help me out, buddy, I'm calling from the drunk tank, not far from your place.
I've got no money, I need fifty-six dollars for them to let me go.
The man promises, hangs up, and gathering the last of his strength, gets up and starts slowly getting dressed, trying not to fall over.
Where to?!
He honestly explains the situation.
His wife takes a long hard look at his puffy face and says:
Take a hundred and twelve dollars!

notes: Sobering-up station is the Ausnüchterungszelle; 156 and 312 roubles became 56 and 112 euros to keep the doubling. All narration and lines kept. Split-screen call, then a cut to the bedroom; both men wear red noses and stubble so the wife's look at his face pays off.
title: Hilf mir, Kumpel

lines.text: Ein Mann wacht morgens mit dem schlimmsten Kater seines Lebens vom Klingeln des Telefons auf.
Es ruft ein Freund an, den er lange nicht gesehen hat.
Von wo rufst du an?
Hilf mir, Kumpel, ich rufe aus der Ausnüchterungszelle an, nicht weit von dir.
Ich hab kein Geld, ich brauche sechsundfünfzig Euro, damit sie mich rauslassen.
Der Mann verspricht es, legt auf, nimmt seine letzten Kräfte zusammen, steht auf und zieht sich langsam an, immer bemüht, nicht umzufallen.
Wohin?!
Er erklärt ehrlich, worum es geht.
Die Frau betrachtet lange sein verquollenes Gesicht und sagt:
Nimm hundertzwölf Euro mit!

notes: Lover is paren (lover role), husband is muzhik. All lines and narration kept; 'the husband walked into the room' is shown by his entrance. Four scenes follow the story: in bed, the statue trick, the kitchen at night, back to the statue with the sandwich and milk. The powdered lover has white skin and clothes.
title: The Statue

lines.text: A woman and her lover were in bed, when the woman heard her husband getting back.
Quick! Rub baby powder on you and pretend to be a statue.
The lover did that.
Honey, what's this statue doing here?
I saw that the Smiths got one, so I decided to get one as well.
The husband got into bed, and the woman fell asleep.
A few hours later, after checking his wife was asleep, he quietly got up, walked into the kitchen,
made a sandwich and got a glass of milk,
came back, and went to the statue.
Here, have something to eat and drink.
I stood like an idiot for three days at the Smiths, and no one offered me anything to eat!

notes: The Smiths became the Petrovs. Lover is paren, husband is muzhik. All lines and narration kept; the husband's arrival is shown by his entrance. Four scenes: in bed, the statue trick, the kitchen at night, back to the statue with the sandwich and milk. The powdered lover has white skin and clothes.
title: Статуя

lines.text: Женщина с любовником были в постели, когда она услышала, что возвращается муж.
Быстро! Натрись детской присыпкой и притворись статуей.
Любовник так и сделал.
Дорогая, а что тут делает эта статуя?
Я увидела, что Петровы себе такую купили, и решила тоже завести.
Муж лёг в постель, а жена уснула.
Через несколько часов, убедившись, что жена спит, он тихонько встал, пошёл на кухню,
сделал бутерброд, налил стакан молока,
вернулся и подошёл к статуе.
На, поешь и попей.
Я три дня у Петровых как дурак простоял, и никто мне даже поесть не предложил!

notes: The Smiths became the Schmidts. Lover is paren, husband is muzhik. All lines and narration kept; the husband's arrival is shown by his entrance. Four scenes: in bed, the statue trick, the kitchen at night, back to the statue with the sandwich and milk. The powdered lover has white skin and clothes.
title: Die Statue

lines.text: Eine Frau lag mit ihrem Liebhaber im Bett, als sie hörte, dass ihr Mann nach Hause kam.
Schnell! Reib dich mit Babypuder ein und tu so, als wärst du eine Statue.
Der Liebhaber tat es.
Schatz, was macht denn diese Statue hier?
Ich habe gesehen, dass die Schmidts sich eine geholt haben, also wollte ich auch eine.
Der Mann legte sich ins Bett, und die Frau schlief ein.
Ein paar Stunden später, als er sicher war, dass seine Frau schlief, stand er leise auf, ging in die Küche,
machte ein Butterbrot, holte ein Glas Milch,
kam zurück und ging zur Statue.
Hier, iss und trink was.
Ich habe drei Tage bei den Schmidts wie ein Idiot herumgestanden, und keiner hat mir was zu essen angeboten!

notes: The lady is a woman, so zhena plays the customer instead of the suggested muzhik; the stock boy is paren in an apron. Both narrator lines kept; 'she asked a stock boy' is shown. The frozen chicken prop stands in for the turkey.
title: Bigger Turkeys

lines.text: While picking up a turkey for this Thanksgiving, I overheard this gem.
A lady was picking through the frozen turkeys, but she couldn't find one big enough for her family.
Do these turkeys get any bigger?
No ma'am, they're dead.

notes: Thanksgiving became New Year. The question 'покрупнее не бывают?' means a bigger size; the stock boy hears 'will they get bigger' and answers that they won't grow any more, they are dead. Zhena plays the lady, paren the stock boy in an apron; the frozen chicken prop stands in for the turkey.
title: Индейки покрупнее

lines.text: Покупал я индейку к Новому году и подслушал вот такой перл.
Одна дама перебирала замороженных индеек, но никак не могла найти достаточно большую для своей семьи.
А покрупнее эти индейки не бывают?
Нет, женщина, крупнее они уже не станут, они мёртвые.

notes: Thanksgiving became Christmas; 'Werden die noch größer?' keeps both readings. Zhena plays the lady, paren the stock boy in an apron; the frozen chicken prop stands in for the turkey.
title: Größere Truthähne

lines.text: Als ich für Weihnachten einen Truthahn kaufte, habe ich diese Perle mitgehört.
Eine Dame wühlte in den tiefgefrorenen Truthähnen, fand aber keinen, der groß genug für ihre Familie war.
Werden die Truthähne noch größer?
Nein, gnädige Frau, die sind tot.

Have you ever been present at a childbirth before?
Yes, just once.
What was it like?
It was dark, then suddenly very bright.

Waren Sie schon einmal bei einer Geburt dabei?
Ja, ein einziges Mal.
Und wie war es?
Erst war es dunkel, dann plötzlich ganz hell.
